The levels, and the first table in the game that is a FARM rather than a habitat. Everything out here lives off a crop or off the things that eat one: Beast in the hedges and the stubble, Terra in the ploughing, Gale over open ground, and one Spark, because the telegraph runs the length of this road and Route 7 North is where that pays off.

SIXTY OF EVERY HUNDRED KIN HERE ARE BEAST-TYPED AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. Beast is the one type in the chart that is neutral against all three starters both ways, so a table built on it cannot lock a starter out the way the wetlands nearly locked out Verdant -- Chitin and Venom each resist Verdant AND hit it double, and Route 6 measured forty per cent for a Bramblehusk before it was rebuilt. The identity is carried by the SECOND types instead: Verdant on Bristlebuck, Terra on Burrowen and Silthopper, Gale on Kestrelle, Chitin on one small Nettlebug slot.

MEASURED, not guessed at. Levels are 24-28 against a team-raising player who leaves Mirehaven at 29, which is the two-to-four-under rule every table since the third pass has followed. At that level, novice play, no items, one Kin in front: Bramblehusk 71, Blazelynx 96, Brookmaw 81. Route 5 sits at 69 and Route 6 at 62, so this is the kindest route table in the second half of the game, which is deliberate -- it is the longest walk in Caelora and nobody should be doing it in a clinic queue.

The water table is the drains. It is gentler again on purpose: a player wading a cut is taking a shortcut and paying for it in time, and a shortcut that also kills you is not a choice anybody makes twice.
